transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. How can I help you today?
Hello, Dr. Smith. My mind just won’t stop going over everything that could go wrong at work, and I can’t seem to turn the worrying off anymore. It has just become too much for me to handle on my own.

Do you feel anxious only when you're in or thinking about specific situations, like being in public or speaking in front of people, or is your worry more general and not tied to particular circumstances?

It’s definitely more general and constant rather than being tied to specific situations like public speaking. While a lot of it started with my work responsibilities, it has spilled over into my personal life, like worrying about my nieces' college savings while I'm just trying to relax in my garden. It feels like this uncontrollable background noise of "what ifs" that I just can't seem to turn off.
How long have you been feeling this way, and is it present most days for at least several months?

These feelings have been building up for a little over a year now, ever since I took on the lead role for our library's digital preservation and oral history project. It has definitely been a constant, near-daily struggle for me throughout this entire period.
In addition to constant worry, do you also experience physical symptoms like restlessness, being easily fatigued, or trouble concentrating?

Yes, my concentration has been terrible—my mind constantly drifts off when I try to read or catalog recordings, and it even goes completely blank during meetings. I also get really restless and find myself pacing the kitchen when the worries start, though I haven't noticed feeling particularly fatigued.
